hook.text: One husband, one wife? That's just one option. Across cultures, marriage takes radically different forms.

buildup.text: Monogamy, polygyny (multiple wives), polyandry (multiple husbands), and group marriage all exist ethnographically.

discovery.text: Marriage is rarely about love alone. It creates alliances between families, transfers wealth, and secures labor.

twist.text: Lévi-Strauss argued that marriage is fundamentally about exchange — groups give and receive partners to build ties.

climax.text: Marriage systems reveal that this most personal institution is actually a deeply political and economic one.

punchline.text: Marriage binds families, not just individuals.

details.summary: Marriage systems vary enormously across cultures — from monogamy to polygyny (multiple wives) to polyandry (multiple husbands). Marriage is rarely just a romantic union; it creates alliances between families, transfers property, establishes legitimate offspring, and reorganizes social groups.
details.whyItMatters: Cross-cultural marriage diversity shows that no single marriage form is natural or universal. Understanding marriage as a flexible social institution challenges ethnocentric assumptions and informs debates about marriage equality.
takeaways: Marriage systems include monogamy, polygyny, and polyandry
Marriage creates alliances, transfers property, and legitimizes offspring
No single marriage form is natural or universally practiced

faq.question: Is monogamy the most common marriage system globally?
faq.answer: No. The majority of documented societies permit polygyny. However, in practice most marriages are monogamous even in polygynous societies because few men can afford multiple wives. Serial monogamy — marrying sequentially — is extremely common worldwide.

faq.question: Why does polyandry exist in some societies?
faq.answer: Polyandry typically appears where land is scarce and inheritance must not be divided. Brothers sharing one wife keeps family property intact. Fraternal polyandry in Tibet and Nepal is the best-documented example, tied directly to land pressure.
